root_cause: The production pricing page returned HTTP 200 with full HTML, but the verifier waited for generic body visibility before waiting for the pricing runtime ready-v3 marker. Under responsive/runtime initialization that generic visibility gate could time out even though the page and pricing controls were present. The same closure also exposed syntax-coupled actionability replays: safe pointer behavior had evolved to page.mouse.click over checked geometry while regressions still required locator.click and a specific callback variable name.
prevention_rule: Production interaction proofs must wait on the product-specific readiness contract and target control visibility, not generic body visibility. Generic page readiness must never block a stronger domain-specific ready marker. Regression assertions about generic readiness must be phase-scoped: forbid body gating before ready-v3, but allow body visibility checks after a deliberate route navigation. Keep production-readiness and actionability replays semantic: assert ready-v3 before interactions, verified control geometry, deterministic positioning and real Playwright pointer input, not incidental source spelling. Prefer direct structural/semantic assertions for stable contract tokens and behavior; do not encode incidental callback names or regex-sensitive source spelling as production truth.
evidence: GET /prijzen?interaction_proof=<sha> returned HTTP 200 with full pricing HTML while body visibility wait timed out.

invariants: pricing ready-v3 marker is authoritative readiness
loss lifecycle control must become visible

failed_approaches: The first regression forbade every body visibility wait in the verifier, accidentally rejecting the legitimate post-navigation English-route body wait. Readiness invariants must be scoped to the pre-runtime-ready phase.
Coupling readiness replay to exact callback names and one click API caused a false negative after equivalent safer pointer implementation evolved.

Using exact source-code regexes for locator spelling/callback syntax caused false-negative historical replay even though the semantic target, geometry checks and real Playwright pointer action were present.
